descriptionChirho: Qal: to stick or adhere physically, of tongue to palate, skin to bones, garments, disease, or objects clinging together.
Qal: to cling to a person, to God, or to a group in loyalty, devotion, or covenant faithfulness; to hold fast relationally.
Pual/Hofal: to be stuck together, joined, or made to cling; the passive of physical adhesion.
Hifil (causative adhesion): to cause something to stick or cling, to make adhere; used of God making a curse or plague cling to someone.
Hifil (pursuit): to press hard after, pursue closely and overtake; used of military pursuit and of calamity catching up to someone.
